sources.title: Comparative Analysis of Distributed Caching Algorithms: Performance ...
sources.snippet: III-B Least Frequently Used (LFU) LFU evicts items with the lowest access frequency when cache capacity is reached. This approach theoretically outperforms LRU for workloads with stable popularity distributions but suffers from "cache pollution" when access patterns evolve over time.

sources.title: An overview of analysis methods and evaluation results for caching ...
sources.snippet: They use a set of information per object, such as the size, popularity, expected costs and benefits for delivering an object from the cache. On that basis, scores are computed for the relevance of objects, where those with highest scores are preferred as cache content.

sources.title: PDF Adaptive Online Cache Capacity Optimization via Lightweight Working Set ...
sources.snippet: Abstract Big data applications extensively use cache techniques to accelerate data access. A key challenge for improving cache utilization is provisioning a suitable cache size to fit the dynamic working set size (WSS) and understanding the related item repetition ratio (IRR) of the trace.

sources.title: Cache-Oblivious Implicit Predecessor Dictionaries with the Working Set Property
sources.snippet: In this paper we present an implicit dynamic dictionary with the working-set property, supporting insert(e) and delete(e) in O(log n) time, predecessor(e) in O(log l_{p(e)}) time, successor(e) in O(log l_{s(e)}) time and search(e) in O(log min(l_{p(e)},l_{e}, l_{s(e)})) time, where n is the number of elements stored in the dictionary, l_{e} is the number of distinct elements searched for since element e was last searched for and p(e) and s(e) are the predecessor and successor of e, respectively.
